notes: Sourced from NEC's official English user's manual for the PX2000UL (hosted on Sharp's manual-download domain, sharp-displays.jp.sharp) — terminal panel diagram/labels on p.8 and full technical spec table on p.78-79 — cross-checked against Sharp NEC Display Solutions of America's own 2-page product spec sheet (PDF, Cat.No. 25.NEC.80.GL.UN.359, Rev 09.24.21). Both are manufacturer-authored. Notes/caveats: (1) This projector ships lens-less; a separate NP45ZL/NP46ZL/NP47ZL/NP48ZL/NP49ZL zoom lens must be purchased. (2) Power spec is 200-240V AC only — there is no 100-120V North American variant, so a step-up/step-down consideration applies for some markets. (3) Variant "NP-PX2000UL-47ZL" bundles the NP47ZL lens preinstalled but is otherwise the same electronics/I-O as the base NP-PX2000UL modeled here. (4) The AC IN connector sub-type (assumed IEC C19) is an inference, not a literal manual label — see port note. (5) DisplayPort grade (1.2) is likewise inferred from the stated 5.4Gbps/4-lane data rate rather than an explicit "DP 1.2" label. (6) No USB port exists on this unit (confirmed absent from both the manual and datasheet). (7) Unit is a large floor/ceiling-mount installation projector (112.4 lbs / 51 kg body only), not a rack-mountable chassis, so rackUnits is omitted. (8) Branded "NEC" on the physical unit; the corporate/legal seller is Sharp NEC Display Solutions of America, Inc. — reflecting the "Sharp/NEC" naming in the request.

ports.name: COMPUTER IN
ports.note: Mini D-Sub 15-pin analog RGB input; datasheet lists it as 'RGB1 (analog)' and notes it also accepts component video via NEC's optional ADP-CV1E adapter cable.

ports.name: MONITOR OUT
ports.note: Mini D-Sub 15-pin analog RGB loop-through output.

ports.name: BNC IN
ports.note: Group of 5 BNC jacks (R/Cr/Cv, G/Y/Y, B/Cb/C, H, V) forming one switchable analog RGBHV / component / composite input; datasheet calls it 'RGB2 (analog) 5BNC'.

ports.name: DisplayPort IN
ports.note: 20-pin DisplayPort, HDCP 1.3/1.4. Grade inferred (not stated by name) from the manual's listed data rate of 5.4/2.7/1.62 Gbps over 1/2/4 lanes, i.e. HBR2 = DisplayPort 1.2 signaling.

ports.name: DVI-D
ports.note: Digital video input, HDCP 1.4/2.2. No bandwidth grade scale applies to DVI in this schema.

ports.name: HDBaseT/LAN
ports.note: Single RJ-45 jack; manual specifies 100BASE-TX. Carries HDBaseT video/control extension (input) plus LAN-based control, monitoring and remote-control passthrough on the same physical port.

ports.name: SDI IN
ports.note: Labeled '3G/HD/SD-SDI IN Terminal (BNC)'; supports SD-SDI, HD-SDI and 3G-SDI up to 1080p50/60.

ports.name: SDI OUT
ports.note: Labeled '3G/HD/SD-SDI OUT Terminal (BNC)'; loop-through of the SDI input signal.

ports.name: REMOTE
ports.note: 3.5mm stereo mini jack for wired remote control (disables IR sensor when connected).

ports.name: PC CONTROL
ports.note: D-Sub 9-pin serial control port (RS-232C, full duplex, 9600bps).

ports.name: TRIGGER 1
ports.note: One of two 3.5mm stereo mini screen-trigger outputs (panel is labeled 'TRIGGER 1/2').

ports.name: TRIGGER 2
ports.note: Second of two 3.5mm stereo mini screen-trigger outputs (panel is labeled 'TRIGGER 1/2').

ports.name: AC IN
ports.note: Power inlet. Rated 200-240V AC 50/60Hz only (no 100-120V support), 9.7A, up to ~1922W (Boost mode). The manual does not print the exact IEC inlet sub-type; C19 (high-current) is inferred because NEC specifies a power cord 'rated 15A or higher' against the 9.7A nameplate draw, which exceeds the typical 10A headroom of a standard C13/C14 inlet. Treat this one connector pick as a medium-confidence inference within an otherwise fully-confirmed source.
